facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: That Hanuma with great strength crossed the insurmountable ocean without becoming tired and viewed the city of Lanka located on the peak of Mount Trikuta.
facts.text: In the Valmiki Ramayana, the island city of Lanka is described as situated across the southern ocean at a distance of one hundred yojanas from the mainland.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: sa saagaram anaadR^ishhyam atikramya mahaabalaH | trikuuTa shikhare lankaam sthitaam svastho dadarsha ha ||
facts.text: The Sundara Kanda specifically records that Ravana's fortified capital of Lanka was built on the summit of Mount Trikuta.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Situated upon the line which passes through the haunt of the rakshasas and the mountain which is the seat of the gods...
facts.text: The classical Sanskrit astronomical treatise Surya Siddhanta defines Lanka as an astronomical baseline city situated on the terrestrial equator at zero degrees latitude.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Ravana was an ordinary human being, as the epic expressly says so. And Lanka was situated in the Vindhyas. Thus Rama had not crossed the Narbada.
facts.source_name: H. D. Sankalia, Ramayana: Myth or Reality?
facts.text: Archaeologist H. D. Sankalia argued in 1973 that the Lanka of the original Ramayana was situated in the Vindhya mountain range and Chota Nagpur plateau in Central India rather than the island of Sri Lanka, a proposition rejected by mainstream traditional scholars who identify Lanka with the southern island.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Lanka was regarded as the city at the intersection of the Equatorial line and the Prime Meridian. Today's Sri Lanka is not the one referenced in the ancient texts, according to Indian astronomers.
facts.text: Astronomers and historians highlight a geographic contradiction because the modern island of Sri Lanka lies between 5 and 10 degrees north latitude, whereas ancient Indian astronomical calculations fixed Lanka strictly on the equator along the Ujjain meridian.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The ruins of the capital built by the parricidal King Kassapa I (477–95) lie on the steep slopes and at the summit of a granite peak standing some 180m high.
facts.text: Archaeological excavations and historical records document that the rock fortress and royal palace at Sigiriya were constructed by King Kashyapa I during his reign from 477 CE to 495 CE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The first inhabitants of the Sigiriya region were the Mesolithic humans who belonged to prehistoric times of Sri Lanka as revealed from the excavation and investigations done in nearby caves in proximity to the Sigiriya summit...
facts.text: Archaeological surveys at the Aligala rock shelter on the eastern slopes of Sigiriya yielded microlithic tools demonstrating prehistoric human occupation dating back approximately 5,500 years before present.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Known for its stunning rock fortress, Sigiriya is a UNESCO World Heritage Site that is also believed to be one of the places where Ravana kept Sita captive.
facts.text: Local Sri Lankan folklore and modern tourism narratives identify Sigiriya as the mythological palace fortress of Ravana named Alakamandava.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Sita refused to live in Ravana's palace. She stayed in the grove, seated under a simsapa tree.
facts.text: In the Sundara Kanda of the Valmiki Ramayana, Ashoka Vatika is described as an imperial garden enclosed by walls and filled with Ashoka, Champaka, and Shimshapa trees where Sita was held captive.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: The Hakgala Botanical Gardens was one of the pleasure gardens of King Ravana... This is the exotic pleasure garden where King Ravana kept the depressed Sita, insisting that she marries him.
facts.text: Popular Sri Lankan pilgrimage traditions identify Hakgala Botanical Garden and the adjacent village of Seetha Eliya as the historical location of Ashoka Vatika.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The garden was established in 1861, under the curation of William Purdie, initially as an experimental cultivation of Cinchona, a source of quinine against malaria.
facts.source_name: Department of National Botanic Gardens, Sri Lanka
facts.text: Historical records indicate that the Hakgala site was formally established by British colonial botanists in 1861 CE as an experimental reserve for cultivating medicinal Cinchona plants.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: On the rock face across the stream are circular depressions said to be the footprints of Lord Hanuman.
facts.text: Devotees at the Seetha Amman Temple in Seetha Eliya identify round depressions in the riverside rock surface as the physical footprints of Hanuman.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Sri Lanka was known to Indians of the olden days as Simhala or Tamraparni, and not as Lanka.
facts.text: Epigraphists emphasize that ancient inscriptions and Pali chronicles refer to the island as Tambapanni and Simhala, leading historians to dispute the antiquity of Sri Lanka's Ramayana place names while local tradition maintains they preserve genuine epic geography.
